brief.title: Election update: Friday, November 13 (morning)
brief.markdown:
# Election update: Friday, November 13 (morning)

## Bottom line
Every governor's race is now decided. Democrats hold 30 governorships to Republicans' 20, counting the 14 states with no race this year, up from 24 before the election ([governor table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_gubernatorial_elections)). The House results table marks 426 races called: D 257, R 169, with 218 needed for a majority; the parse again missed Delaware's at-large seat, held by Rep. Sarah McBride (D), so the Democratic count is one low ([House table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)). The Senate stands at D 55, R 44, counting seats not up, with Alaska the last uncalled race ([Senate table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)). Three seats rated Solid R came in within 5 points; Republicans held all three.

## Called since the last update
- **Flip (1, D):** GOV-AK, where Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins (D) topped 50%, so no ranked-choice tabulation is needed, Alaska Public Media reports ([Alaska Public Media](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMixgFBVV95cUxNdEVQWklvTk9YZHdxMTF2eUdBSnpCNzk4MENqenFLWXRQREpub2tnZXI0M1VsS1luM24zTERRQzVjd1k3dno2dWZMMkhyWEkzbFpJdmg0ZWI1eEo0TzZ6UXduVG1nb2djY3huZmFycmhkWWwxMzFhbE1tUVZHdEJkY1NYNV8zRUNCZlc4RW1zZGpOMnJCUVZoRFZWeDNqeHBjcFBMT25PSTJlSExmYXlYTTJVbjBPUU51cXZzZEYwb2FFYmh6aUE?oc=5)). The seat was held by Gov. Mike Dunleavy (R).
- **Hold (1, D):** GOV-KS, where Cindy Holscher (D) defeated Ty Masterson (R) in a seat rated Tilt R, NBC News reports ([NBC News](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivAFBVV95cUxOdzJIZE9XQmw3bVRsVDc4RmdDdUVPLU91NVJJdnBpbFI5QkROWUt3S096WEZfakYwRTNrM3pSUkk4YThwbF9vemZvcXVjQ2ppXzgxMTF6aHhYOEtvMklGRWFsNnYyNlkwQm51YW1IQkR3djZFeXlzUDdRMlBJb0FybDZLdl9KaS1ZYm16VVZGLXJuQ1lXVldaMHVTZGJJRlBiVUhhNW0yZVlkVGNYRUZXeGY1a3RsYnBSODFzRw?oc=5)); PBS also reports her win ([PBS](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwgFBVV95cUxNS0xoelhvSE5mQWkwX3ZETXVYRk9NYUpuY1VDbGVaM19QSGh1Z05kaEhQM2RvSHdldXFDX0FqTm1uMS10eEl6Y2xHX2hhN1JXaFcxelB6TFJIb2pza1B0VEJhSUUzY0RCaTBNX0ZjdE9UODdmemM3NHBTN290TTAzYXB4YTNCWW5ybE83NWR1VWxTRnpOX19vS1JabldVbGtxZTNETFhIdDNKU0lxck4zN1RhQzdfYlRrUHBXWmo4cnRKUQ?oc=5)).
- No House or Senate race was called.

## Still uncalled
One line for every competitive race the table hasn't marked called: Senate first, then House. No governor race is left.
- **SEN-AK** (Tossup): Mary Peltola (D) extended her lead over Sen. Dan Sullivan (R), Alaska Public Media reports ([Alaska Public Media](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMixgFBVV95cUxNdEVQWklvTk9YZHdxMTF2eUdBSnpCNzk4MENqenFLWXRQREpub2tnZXI0M1VsS1luM24zTERRQzVjd1k3dno2dWZMMkhyWEkzbFpJdmg0ZWI1eEo0TzZ6UXduVG1nb2djY3huZmFycmhkWWwxMzFhbE1tUVZHdEJkY1NYNV8zRUNCZlc4RW1zZGpOMnJCUVZoRFZWeDNqeHBjcFBMT25PSTJlSExmYXlYTTJVbjBPUU51cXZzZEYwb2FFYmh6aUE?oc=5)); the BBC explains why Alaska's count takes so long ([BBC](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiW0FVX3lxTE0teVRDTDFRRTFTc19RMVA0WnNBVWswSV9ad05pZ0Uxa19SMVVoMkdPY0JYeXcwaGhHWk8tanNycW5qWFRQMnZhaEFsTkhFNmlVcWNKdzVobW5xbTQ?oc=5)).
- **HOU-AK-AL** (Lean R): Rep. Nick Begich III (R) was near victory as of Wednesday's count, the Alaska Beacon reported ([Alaska Beacon](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivgFBVV95cUxPaDRheGpFczN3anVBdVFMSHZPMTNMdm1Gd05aNGZGVmpJWG53RTY4RWVWQ3FWSkpUaFAzWXFLd2l4VmEtMGQ3YXRhdGhpSWhiemtfT1dmcFRTa3ItQ1JxWnFIa1dfZEVCcGFjTklycDBOZkVZTjBSNEg1WGgyZFpramNnLVdIeTlOOUJXbHZ4aGo5eEhRQXpzaUFaOTR4c1dOcVotRVlBTlc0UkM3TWEzWmpMN1JVbjdWZndNRFJR?oc=5)).
- **HOU-NC-05** (Likely R): with provisional ballots counted, Democrats are poised to pick up the seat, WUNC reports; AP has not called it ([WUNC](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **HOU-NC-07** (Likely R): still too close to call, Carolina Public Press reports ([Carolina Public Press](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwwFBVV95cUxNZWE4NjY2T1d6WUNIQlBKa2VmZXh3WGNQc2p6TkNBcmgyaF84R1M4ZjFZd2Y2VlcxOU9maEVkT2hvZkZOX3l4U2Z4THlyNDl0WHB5Vy1wN29MS0NCcnRvSTNjUF9SOVdudlNuZU8yNFBLVnYyX3dwV0sxb01pRHBXQjdUWWt4ZjJHc3lxUWVRWWx1cU9tdHF4OE9GTkE2WElYY3FzMzJiZmpidlRNaWhrdTV0SWc3Qk9HWE94ZzNZanBkVEE?oc=5)); the margin is within recount range, per the Charlotte Observer ([Charlotte Observer](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **HOU-MN-01** (Lean R): still uncalled; Minnesota is headed for a jump in recounts ([KSTP](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipwFBVV95cUxNSDRZYzJvQ19XMnNDWWRISlVJSkdKbk9CRVd1czFhQUlmUHVoZXp4Y3oxVnREQ0I5QUYtWExmLUVBVFpyMkJTeHFDd3h3czZBVzNJVXJCZElLbjhQNGx6OWkzYXhHdF9xYWFDNXNZRkt5NmZQNHI1QXEzZTY0M2FZbU9Rd21hYndCMnI2MGt6SEt2MER2dU1xRjBKX3lhWUVQRFNvU3FTTQ?oc=5)).
- **Safe seats:** 4 seats rated safe are not yet marked in the table. That is table lag, not close races ([full list](https://jakeworcester-byte.github.io/political-tracker/#results)).

## Recounts and certification
- **North Carolina:** WCNC lays out the canvass and recount steps ahead for the state's close races ([WCNC](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **Kansas:** the state board's canvass is Nov. 16, and the recount-request deadline is 5 p.m. Nov. 17 ([KWCH](https://www.kwch.com/2026/11/10/nearly-week-after-midterm-election-governors-race-is-still-too-close-call/)).
- **New Hampshire:** 16 recounts are under way for state House races ([New Hampshire Bulletin](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimwFBVV95cUxQUnJOMUlRQm5EdnFDTGR4TkZHbzJhSGVtLS1jVmFZa0c4cWFYOHd1TUZGb3I5M19CT3ZwLXk2WjJMa3kwQzBhZ3BPMFBmY3VZdmczNkRkcmFXbWxLSDg5bkJqalhMakRObG9hWDFYbnM4MmVNdk5EQ3lpZFNfYXJ1T2hxZkFONEpXQ19PS01ScFAxQ3ExYlNtVUQtWQ?oc=5)).

## Legal and federal action
- **Alaska:** a judge ruled the Peltola campaign's request for rejected-absentee ballot data "not reasonable," Alaska's News Source reports ([Alaska's News Source](https://news.google.?oc=5)); Fox News reports she keeps a narrow lead after the loss in court ([Fox News](https://news.google.?oc=5)).
- **Federal dockets:** CourtListener shows activity in 38 election-related federal dockets since Nov. 10, including the FL-27 recount suit, Rodriguez v. Garcia ([CourtListener](https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/75084109/rodriguez-v-garcia-et-al/)).

## What voters said
- **Turnout:** NPR identifies two turnout trends that explain results across the South ([NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/13/nx-s1-6038701/midterm-election-voter-turnout-south)).
- **Analysis:** Brookings argues the historic wins show the vote was about more than prices ([Brookings](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimwFBVV95cUxPTjF2RWVOMkd1TXZIenY4akhPTExkakdLdmZycGxUVHlFMkhIRkZjOWw4MVV0TVg5VmhTU2lJVEpjUzFjNmwtZlBWTzhIUXhJY1ZGSmtzSmlUc0p3cjR3Nnlra002NzQwVmd4UjllY2xIREc1QTFySkVHcklXWG9ja2E1MDBQS240Uk5oYjhNVmE2bjdjWXNlazliMA?oc=5)). No new voter-file read from Ralston or Bitzer is in today's leads.

## Coverage note
- **Parser:** the Senate (35) and governor (36) tables parsed fully and the parser check is healthy. The House table parsed 434 of 435 rows for a second day; Delaware's at-large row is missed, so the House Democratic count is one low. The parser fix is left for an attended session.
- **Court records:** CourtListener used (4 requests; 38 election dockets and 1 opinion).
- **Scorecard:** 95.2% of competitive races called; Lessons learned returns weekly (next around Nov. 16).
